name: painprep-mcp-server

tools.name: get_procedure_list
tools.description: Returns the full catalog of interventional pain medicine procedures, grouped by category. Each entry includes the procedure id (used by other tools), display name, short name, and headline CPT code(s). Optionally filter by a category id or name. FREE tier.

category.description: Optional category filter (id like "epidural" or label like "Epidural Injections").

tools.name: get_cpt_codes
tools.description: Given a procedure (name, id, or CPT code), returns the primary CPT code(s), add-on codes, work RVUs, typical facility setting (office/ASC/hospital), and billing notes. FREE tier.

procedure.description: Procedure name, id, or a CPT code to look up.

tools.name: get_medicare_checklist
tools.description: Given a procedure, returns the full Medicare/LCD documentation checklist: required documentation items with rationale and suggested chart wording, top denial triggers, and pre-submission admin checks. Flags items that are commonly missed. PREMIUM tier.

procedure.description: Procedure name, id, or CPT code.

tools.name: get_icd10_codes
tools.description: Given a procedure, returns the approved/supportive ICD-10 diagnosis codes, codes to AVOID (common denial triggers), and coding tips for medical-necessity support. PREMIUM tier.

procedure.description: Procedure name, id, or CPT code.

tools.name: get_contraindications
tools.description: Given a procedure, returns its bleeding-risk level and the ASRA-aligned anticoagulant/antiplatelet stop-and-restart guidance (per agent), special considerations, and general pre-procedure safety checks. Always verify against the current ASRA guidelines and institutional policy. PREMIUM tier.

procedure.description: Procedure name, id, or CPT code.

tools.name: get_prior_auth_letter
tools.description: Generates a formal, payer-ready prior-authorization / medical-necessity letter for a procedure, merging supplied patient and clinical details with the procedure’s CPT codes, recommended primary ICD-10 code, evidence grade, and necessity rationale. Any field left unspecified is rendered as a clearly-marked fill-in blank. The structured medical-necessity worksheet is appended when available. PREMIUM tier.

procedure.description: Procedure name, id, or CPT code.

icd10.description: Primary ICD-10 code; defaults to the recommended primary code.

painScore.description: Pain score, e.g. "7/10 at rest, 9/10 with activity".

conservativeCare.description: Failed conservative care with durations, e.g. "8 weeks PT, NSAIDs x6 weeks".

includeWorksheet.description: Append the structured medical-necessity worksheet template (default true).

tools.name: get_denial_reasons
tools.description: Given a procedure, returns the common payer denial reasons with their relative frequency, the concrete fix/remedy for each, and a ready-to-adapt appeal letter snippet. PREMIUM tier.

procedure.description: Procedure name, id, or CPT code.

tools.name: get_research_evidence
tools.description: Given a procedure, returns the overall evidence grade, a summary of the evidence base, and the key supporting studies (title, journal, year, and headline finding) for use in notes and appeals. PREMIUM tier.

procedure.description: Procedure name, id, or CPT code.

tools.name: check_documentation_completeness
tools.description: Given a procedure and the list of items already documented in the chart, audits the note against the Medicare required-documentation checklist and returns what is satisfied, what is still missing (with rationale and suggested wording), a spotlight on commonly-missed gaps, and an overall completeness score. PREMIUM tier.

procedure.description: Procedure name, id, or CPT code.

documented.description: Items already documented — checklist item ids or free-text phrases (e.g. "MRI findings", "conservative care 8 weeks").

instructions: PainPrep provides interventional pain medicine reference data: procedure catalog, CPT/ICD-10 coding, Medicare documentation checklists, ASRA anticoagulation guidance, prior-authorization letters, denial appeals, and research evidence. Start with get_procedure_list to discover procedure ids, then call the specific tool. Tools accept a procedure name, id, or CPT code. This is clinical decision-support, not medical advice — a licensed clinician must review all output.
